title: Is there a simple solution for this tall character parallax problem?

posts.author: Star_Anise
posts.body:
Hello, I'm using RPG Maker for the first time as an artist, so I've been utilizing a lot of plugins and learning how they work. I'm ironing out issues before diving into little details and had a question about this problem when parallaxing:
I understand the limitations with using RPG Maker with larger sprites, but I'm working off the grid tiles as best I can. I thought I saw a plugin floating around that sets when the player is above a certain Y the the parallax image can be below/behind. I figured I can cheese a lot of areas to not have the character pass through the parallax layer, but I'd prefer to have a little freedom with it. Any advice to this problem would be greatly appreciated.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Rgblu said:
I thought I saw a plugin floating around that sets when the player is above a certain Y the the parallax image can be below/behind
Click to expand...
There
is
one that comes with MV in the dlc folder, but I am not sure for MZ. It likely does exist for MZ too, but maybe doesn't come with the editor itself. Regardless, that one that comes with MV is more pertaining to tiles, and not images bound to the map.
You'd need to tell us how you are binding the images to the map.
One thing you can do is manually convert the layer by using an event that switches the priority of the tree when the player crosses the event, but could be tedious depending on the detailing of your game.
Hopefully someone with more experience with this can provide you a better answer.
However
Rgblu said:
I'm using RPG Maker for the first time
Click to expand...
If I may, I'd like to share some unrelated advice.
If you are a beginner with RPG Maker, this sounds like you are setting yourself up for failure; either you will get burnt out, frustrated, or spend years making an unoptimized mess.
I highly recommend you spend some time with the editor in it's default state; practically no plugins, and just using the functionality that exists in RPG Maker.
Make a short game - just like, an hour long more or less. Don't set out for making something fun or even interesting. Set out with the goal of learning.
I would advise maybe doing 2 games like this; 1 to learn basic functions of the engine, and another about the same size but to learn plugins, build up your library of such plugins, as well as various assets and tools to assist in making games.
But, you do you.
Good luck!

This is exactly what I did! The kind of advice I got a few years ago was just like this.
So that's what I did.
First game, just an hour long, made with no plugins.
So I'm someone who sort of avoided a lot of common issues new developer issues that people seem to talk about all the time.
Since I didn't experience those problems myself, it's hard to say if I'd have learned more doing it the hard way, learning from mistakes, but I'll probably never know.
Rgblu said:
I thought I saw a plugin floating around that sets when the player is above a certain Y the the parallax image can be below/behind.
Click to expand...
I'm using GridFree Doodads (Yanfly/VisuStella; I'm technically using the MV version but this is a project in MZ).
This tool lets you place an image of any size and freely adjust/place it directly into your game using an in-game menu. It has its own issues that I personally don't understand.
Here are some pictures of a test room I made trying to figure out how to smoothly let my character walk around, behind, and in front of some boxes for my game. It's RPG Maker MV, and the pics are from the game itself so you can't see the grid, but trust me it is just RPG Maker on a 48x48 tile grid. My characters/npcs are technically 32x40px but they tend to not use the full width so they are considerably taller than they are wide.
Spoiler:
Grid-Free Doodads plugin screenshots
Each box in the room is a "doodad" made with the GridFree Doodads plugin.
Which is just a .png somewhere in your img folder that you can easily decorate your game with.
You have quite a bit of control over where to set the anchor and point where the image will show above/behind the character.
I've put one box on the upper layer (in the last pic) and this makes it so any npc (or the player character, or followers, etc) will be beneath it.
So if you were using this plugin, you could remove the tree from your parallax (however you're doing that), and instead just have the image as a doodad with this plugin, and place it by hand directly into your game right where you want it, pixel-perfect. The nice part is you can select (to some extent) where you want the anchor to be which is the point on that image where the player would flip from being in front to behind (that Y value you're looking for), and by default it is generally at the bottom center of a doodad. So your tree might have some deep roots that you might want the player to be able to walk over, but this can be handled just by understanding right where the placement is and an artist will have absolutely no trouble figuring this out.
You can freely move your character (or NPCs and other events) in and around your doodads as they have no collision, so you'll have to figure that part out yourself for your own game, even if it is as simple as using tiles that hide beneath your parallax image(s) to control the collision.
Anyway, this plugin seems to fit what you need nicely so I thought I'd suggest it.
